issues.failure_explanation: The paper implicitly expands the y-neighbour coefficient as ((j\pm1)^2-1/4)=(j^2-1/4)\pm2j, but the correct identity is ((j\pm1)^2-1/4)=(j^2-1/4)\pm2j+1. Hence the displayed inner integrand of I_y equals the correct y-part integrand minus the term v(x_1,x_2+h)/(x_2+h)^2 + v(x_1,x_2-h)/(x_2-h)^2 - 2v(x_1,x_2)/x_2^2 = h^2\partial_2^2[v/x_2^2] + (h^4/6)\int_{-1}^1 \partial_2^4[v(x_1,x_2+\sigma h)/(x_2+\sigma h)^2](1-|\sigma|)^3 d\sigma, which is then dropped from the estimate. The displayed bound for I_y therefore controls a quantity differing from the true y-part of the error by this term, and the proof as written does not establish the stated estimate. The dropped term is O(h^2) in the error and is controlled by the same norms entering C^v, so the theorem's conclusion is correct, but the proof needs the decomposition redone and the extra term estimated.

failure_location.quote: I_y = \sum_{i, j \geq 2} \left(j^2 -\frac{1}{4}\right) \left\{ \int_{\CC^{i,j}_h} \left\{ \left(j^2 -\frac{1}{4}\right)\left[ \frac{v(x_1,x_2\pm h)}{(x_2\pm h)^2} - \dfrac{v(x_1,x_2)}{x_2^2}\right] - x_2^2 \partial^2_{x_2} \left[\frac{v(x_1,x_2)}{x_2^2}\right] + 2j \left[\frac{v(x_1,x_2+ h)}{(x_2+ h)^2} - \frac{v(x_1,x_2- h)}{(x_2- h)^2} \right] - 4 x_2 \partial_{x_2}\left[\frac{v(x_1,x_2)}{x_2^2}\right] \right\} \dd{\x} \right\}^2

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the I_y decomposition with the correct identity ((j\pm1)^2-1/4)=(j^2-1/4)\pm2j+1, retain the extra term v(x_1,x_2+h)/(x_2+h)^2 + v(x_1,x_2-h)/(x_2-h)^2 - 2v(x_1,x_2)/x_2^2 (= h^2\partial_2^2[v/x_2^2] + (h^4/6)\int_{-1}^1 \partial_2^4[v(x_1,x_2+\sigma h)/(x_2+\sigma h)^2](1-|\sigma|)^3 d\sigma) in the inner integrand, and bound it via the same Cauchy-Schwarz and grid-cell estimates (Lemma rem:O(h2), Lemma lem:first-grid-y-n) already used; it is absorbed by the same constant C^v, so the statement and the O(h^2) rate are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:consistency-first-lapl does not establish the stated O(h^2) consistency estimate as written. The estimate itself is correct (the missing term contributes O(h^4 (C^v)^2) to Err_h(v)^2 and is absorbed by C^v), so the consistency theory for \Delta_h^{(1)}, the semi-discrete convergence theorem thm:added-1 and the fully discrete convergence theorem thm:convergence-theta for the first Laplacian remain valid once the proof gap is repaired.
issues.title: Algebraic error in the I_y decomposition drops a term from the first discrete Laplacian's consistency proof
issues.why_classification: The stated estimate, rate, and constant are all correct and survive, but the proof contains a genuine algebraic error in its central decomposition and the dropped term is estimated nowhere in the source; repairing it requires redoing the decomposition and adding a contained (though nontrivial) estimate. No new global proof architecture is needed and no mathematical content is lost, but the repair goes beyond a one-word typo fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $k=3$, summing up \ref{acaret1:porunca3}) and the instance of \ref{acaret1:porunca3}) for $-h$, we get:

issues.failure_explanation: Summing item (iii) with its instance at -h and substituting \sigma\mapsto-\sigma in one of the two integrals yields \varphi(h)+\varphi(-h)-2\varphi(0)=h^2\varphi''(0)+(h^3/2)\int_{-1}^1\varphi'''(h\sigma)(1-|\sigma|)^2 d\sigma, with NO {\rm sgn}(\sigma) factor; the stated identity is false (e.g., for \varphi(\sigma)=\sigma^3 the left side is 0 while the right side equals h^4/2). The identity is never invoked elsewhere in the paper (only items (vi) and (vii) are used, in the two consistency proofs), so no other result is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the spurious {\rm sgn}(\upsigma) factor in item (iv); the corrected identity then follows from item (iii) exactly as the text describes.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed identity inside lemma lem:croytoru_integral is false as stated; since it is never applied, no dependent claim, rate, or guarantee is affected.
issues.title: Spurious sign factor in the symmetric third-order Taylor identity (item (iv) of the Taylor lemmata)
issues.why_classification: A one-word deletion repairs the false identity; the formula is never used, so no substantive claim is lost and no dependent result is touched.

issues.failure_explanation: The change of variables \sigma=s/2-(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t with s\geq0 gives the integration range \sigma\geq-(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t, but the paper integrates over all of \mathbb{R}. For \sigma<-(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t the factor 2\sigma+2(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t is negative and 1+[2\sigma+2(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t]\sqrt t becomes negative, so the integrand displayed is not real-valued on the extended range; the display also drops the Jacobian factor 2 from ds=2 d\sigma. The conclusion M\leq C_{\alpha,T} is unaffected because the integral over the correct range is finite and is bounded by its value at t=T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the lower integration limit -(\alpha+1/2)\sqrt t (or extend by the absolute value of the integrand); the resulting integral is finite and monotone in t, yielding the same bound C_{\alpha,T}.
issues.overall_effect: The final estimate in the proof of lem:stability-exp(alpha-d) is formally ill-defined as displayed; the lemma's conclusion (exponential L^2 stability of the heat semigroup under an exponential weight) is standard and unchanged, so its uses in lem:2-relatii and lem:pseudo-Schwarz-heat remain valid after the local repair.
issues.title: Ill-defined extension of the integration range in the proof of the exponential stability lemma
issues.why_classification: A short, local repair of the integration range restores the proof with no change to the conclusion, the constant, or any dependent result.

issues.failure_explanation: The computed ratio is I(v^{m,n})=\frac{6}{2m^2+1}\frac{\sum_{|j|\leq n}e^{2jh}}{2n+1}+\frac{2}{e^h+1}[\frac{2n}{2n+1}(e^{h/2}-1)^2+\frac{1+e^h}{2n+1}]. For every fixed m the first summand behaves like \frac{6}{2m^2+1}\frac{e^{(2n+1)h}}{(2n+1)(e^{2h}-1)}\to+\infty as n\to\infty, so the stated order of limits does not yield C_h(\rho(h))^2 — along that order I(v^{m,n}) diverges. Taking m\to\infty first (fixed n) and then n\to\infty gives exactly \frac{2}{e^h+1}(e^{h/2}-1)^2=C_h(\rho(h))^2, so the optimality claim is true but the proof's limiting argument is wrong as written.

failure_location.quote: Taking $n$ large enough and then $m\to \infty$, we obtain that the above quantity approaches: \[\frac{2}{e^h+1}\left(e^{h/2}-1\right)^2 = C_h (\rho(h))^2\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the order of the limits: for fixed n let m\to\infty so that the x-dependent term \frac{6}{2m^2+1}\frac{\sum_{|j|\leq n}e^{2jh}}{2n+1} vanishes, then let n\to\infty to obtain C_h(\rho(h))^2.
issues.overall_effect: The sharpness ('C_h is optimal') assertion of prop:lapl-2-poincare is not established by the argument as written; the optimality itself holds, so the discrete exponential stability restoration based on this constant is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong order of limits in the sharpness argument for the second discrete Poincaré constant
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence repair (reversing the order of the two limits) fully restores the optimality proof with no loss; the inequality and the constant are unchanged.
